overview.name: Matthew Florek
overview.headline: Data analysis with a builder's range
overview.shortBio: I am a data analyst who also builds the tools around the analysis: automated workflows, operational systems, geospatial work, and full-stack AI products.
overview.longBio: My background is in finance and business analytics, with experience turning difficult operational information into usable datasets, reports, and repeatable processes. Alongside that work, I build software and experiments of my own—from map-based Android tools to AI products. I like work that rewards both careful analysis and the patience to make a system useful in practice.

projects.title: Operations Grant Database
projects.summary: An Excel and Power Query data platform that unified fragmented grant sources into a reporting backbone with 45+ interconnected pipelines.

details.context: Grant information arrived across fragmented sources, making consistent reporting and historical comparison difficult.
details.contribution: I designed the relational Excel data model, built 45+ Power Query pipelines, and added validation, reconciliation, and historical snapshot layers.
details.outcome: Reporting datasets that once took hours or days to compile could be prepared in minutes, with a more reliable backbone for dashboards and compliance workflows.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy uses reviewed pipeline and timing evidence while withholding internal source systems, stakeholders, URLs, and confidential workflow details.

projects.title: Grant Application Dashboard
projects.summary: An Excel dashboard system integrating 24 grant programs so leadership could see application volume, status, and trends in one place.

details.context: Application reporting was spread across programs and ad-hoc requests, making workload planning dependent on estimates.
details.contribution: I built the relational data model and reporting views in Excel, Power Query, and Power Pivot across 24 grant programs.
details.outcome: Leadership gained current visibility into volume, status, and trends without waiting days for each custom report.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy uses the reviewed 24-program scope and reporting outcomes while withholding program names, screenshots, customer details, URLs, and unreviewed outcomes.

projects.title: Grant Evaluation Workflow Automation
projects.summary: A Power Automate Desktop and JavaScript workflow that extracted evaluation data from a legacy web system and eliminated roughly 320 hours of manual work per run.

details.context: A legacy web process required a team of four to re-enter evaluation data over roughly two weeks.
details.contribution: I built a Power Automate Desktop workflow that navigated the system and used JavaScript to extract the needed data.
details.outcome: The workflow removed the manual entry bottleneck, improved consistency, and made on-demand extraction repeatable—about 320 hours of manual work per execution.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy uses the reviewed 320-hour estimate while withholding system names, URLs, screenshots, customer information, and other unverified details.

projects.title: Title I Comparability Evaluation
projects.summary: A Power Query rules engine that translated federal and state policy into a repeatable Title I comparability review workflow.

details.context: A statewide federal compliance process required specialists to apply detailed policy rules across a large set of districts.
details.contribution: I translated federal legislation and state policy into a structured Power Query evaluation engine.
details.outcome: The workflow filtered out more than 70% of districts automatically and saved approximately 750 specialist hours annually, leaving experts to focus on complex cases.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy uses the reviewed policy, 70% filtering, and 750-hour estimate while withholding employer, program, case, and implementation details.

projects.title: School District Boundary and Census Analysis
projects.summary: A QGIS workflow that reconstructed dissolved Arizona school-district boundaries and prepared corrected files for Census reporting.

details.context: A legally dissolved district was still represented incorrectly in operational and federal boundary records.
details.contribution: I used legal descriptions, county records, and QGIS to reconstruct the boundary changes and prepare corrected files.
details.outcome: The updated boundary submission helped align Census and operational records with the district’s legal absorption by neighboring districts.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy uses the reviewed boundary-reconstruction and Census-submission work while withholding source datasets, map artifacts, customer details, and internal URLs.

projects.title: Metamorphysis.ai
projects.summary: A full-stack resume-intelligence workspace that turns user-owned career information into structured, targeted, ATS-aware documents and workflows.

details.context: Career information is often scattered across static documents and difficult to reuse consistently for a specific opportunity.
details.contribution: I built a Next.js and PostgreSQL workspace with self-hosted authentication, source libraries, draft/report workflows, admin CMS controls, and AI-assisted tailoring.
details.outcome: The product treats experience as reviewable structured assets that can be assembled into targeted documents without losing the underlying source material.

projects.reviewNotes: Confirm the preferred public description and whether the portfolio should identify Matthew as creator, maintainer, or contributor.

projects.title: BettrGrants
projects.summary: An early full-stack SaaS prototype for grant-compliance workflows, with configurable admin tooling and the foundations of a multi-tenant product.

details.context: Grant compliance combines detailed policy, structured information, and recurring workflows that are often managed through fragmented spreadsheets.
details.contribution: I architected a TypeScript/PostgreSQL platform with reusable GUI-driven workflow modules, authentication, onboarding, account management, and billing foundations.
details.outcome: The prototype demonstrated the technical path while clarifying that policy variation, domain detail, and validated customer need were the larger product risks.

projects.reviewNotes: Public copy is intentionally high-level. No public URL was verified, so no link is shown. Ownership language, current status, implementation details, and partner/customer information remain intentionally unspecified.
